questions.stem: What does the room status "VD" usually mean on a housekeeping report?
options: Vacant dirty: no guest, but the room needs cleaning
Very dirty: the guest has left the room in a mess
VIP departure: an important guest is leaving today
Visitor due: a visitor for the guest is coming today

Rooms with Do Not Disturb signs on the door

Rooms needed for early arrivals or VIP guests

options: Knock loudly until the guest answers the door
Do not knock; come back later and follow the property's rules
Open the door quietly and clean round the guest

Heavy items low, chemicals kept apart from clean linen
Dirty linen on the top shelf with the clean towels

At the end of the corridor, out of sight of guests

Knock, say "Housekeeping", wait, and repeat before opening

Bend your knees and go round the bed, not reach over it
Make the bed from one side only to save steps
Keep your legs straight and bend from the waist

Use the dirty sheets to wipe the bathroom floor
Put it straight into the linen bag on the trolley

That the guest's suitcase is under the bed
That the bed has been pushed against the wall

A neat, folded corner that holds the sheet tight and flat
A corner of the bed that is pushed against the wall
A pillow placed at a slant in the corner of the bed

It shows the guest has paid the bill in full

questions.stem: Why do you put toilet cleaner in the bowl at the start of cleaning the bathroom?

So the bowl is dry by the time you reach it
So it has time to work while you clean other parts
So the guest knows the toilet has been cleaned

A cloth kept only for toilets, as the colour code says

The bathroom floor and the inside of the shower

options: Put them in a drawer so the desk looks tidy
Take them to lost property to keep them safe
Read the papers to check they are not rubbish
Leave them where they are and dust round them

questions.stem: In an occupied room, which items may you throw away?
options: Anything on the floor, such as clothes and shoes
Only what is in the waste bins

questions.stem: A guest has checked out and you find a phone charger in the room. What should you do?
options: Keep it, as departed guests do not come back
Use it to charge your own phone until the end of the shift
Hand it in so that it is logged as lost property

options: Politely send them to the front desk to show ID and get a key

options: In the door of the room you are cleaning
On you at all times, on a cord or clip

questions.stem: You are cleaning a room and need to fetch towels from the linen store. What should you do with the room door?
options: Leave it open so you can get back in quickly

questions.stem: What is a "stayover" (occupied) room service?
options: Cleaning a room while the guest is still staying
Cleaning a room after the guest has checked out
Making up an extra bed for a guest's visitor
Leaving the room alone until the guest goes

questions.stem: In an occupied room, how should you treat the guest's clothes left on the bed?
options: Hang them all up in the wardrobe in order of colour
Put them in the laundry bag to be washed
Fold them neatly or leave them, as the rules say

Turning down the air conditioning when guests leave

An evening service to get the room ready for sleep

questions.stem: Which of these is a usual part of turn-down service?
options: Stripping the bed and changing every sheet
Folding back the bed cover and closing the curtains
Moving the guest's suitcase out into the corridor for them
Cleaning the windows and the balcony doors

questions.stem: A family is arriving at a villa this afternoon. Which job is part of getting it ready?
options: Locking every bedroom so the family cannot get in early
Turning off the water so the pipes do not leak
Checking that lights, taps, AC and TV all work
Removing the towels so the family brings their own

questions.stem: Why is a villa's air conditioning switched on for a while before guests arrive?
options: So the rooms are cool and fresh when they arrive
So the electricity bill is higher that month
So that the windows can be left wide open all day long

questions.stem: While cleaning, you find the bathroom tap is dripping. What should you do?
options: Leave it, because the guest will report it if they mind
Tighten it hard with a spanner from the trolley
Put a towel under it so no one hears the drip

questions.stem: Why should faults in a room be reported quickly?
options: So that the room attendant can leave work much earlier
So they are fixed before a guest is upset or hurt
So the guest pays for the repair on checkout
So the room can be marked as clean sooner

questions.stem: When a room is finished, what is the last thing you do before leaving?
options: Check it as a guest would, then update its status
Spray air freshener heavily so it smells clean
Leave the lights and AC on full for the next guest
Leave the door open so the supervisor can look in

questions.stem: Why must the room status be updated as soon as a room is ready?
options: So the guest's bill can be paid by the front desk
So the room attendant's wages can be worked out
So the front desk knows it can give the room to a guest
So the laundry knows how many sheets to wash

questions.stem: Which product must never be used together with a bleach-based bathroom cleaner?
options: Clean, cold water used to rinse the surface

options: Push it down into the bin bag with your hand
Pick it up and put it on the trolley's top shelf
Empty the bin into the linen bag to hide it

questions.stem: How many guests is a "twin" room usually set up for?
options: One guest, in one large double bed
Two guests, sharing one large bed

questions.stem: Why should you count and record the linen and supplies you take for your floor?

Only when the guests phone to ask for it

essays.stem: Describe how to service a departure (check-out) room, from entering the room to updating its status.
essays.modelAnswer: I park my trolley across the doorway, knock, say "Housekeeping", wait and knock again before opening the door. I switch on the lights to check the bulbs, open the curtains and air the room. I check for items left by the guest and for damage or missing items, and report them. I remove rubbish and used glasses. I strip the bed slowly, looking for needles or guest items, and put the linen straight into the linen bag. I check the mattress and its cover for stains and bed bugs, then make the bed with fresh linen to the property's standard. I put toilet cleaner in the toilet, then clean the bathroom from the cleanest parts to the toilet, and the floor last. I restock towels, toilet tissue and amenities. In the bedroom I dust from high to low, clean mirrors and glass, check the minibar, phone, TV, AC and safe, and restock supplies. I vacuum last, working back to the door. I check the room as a guest would, lock it and update its status.
markingPoints: Correct entry: trolley at the door, knock, announce, wait, repeat
Checks for left items, damage and faults; airs the room and removes rubbish
Strips carefully, checks the mattress, makes the bed to standard
Cleans and restocks the bathroom in the right order
Dusts high to low, checks equipment, vacuums last, final check, locks and updates status

essays.stem: Explain how to make a bed with flat sheets and mitred corners.
essays.modelAnswer: I pull the bed out a little if needed, so I can walk round it, and I check the mattress and mattress protector are clean and straight. I put the bottom sheet on with the centre fold down the middle of the bed and the right side up, leaving the same overhang on each side. I tuck it in firmly at the head, then at the foot. To make a mitred corner, I lift the hanging sheet at the side about 30 cm from the corner up onto the mattress, making a slanted fold, tuck in the part that hangs below, then drop the fold down and tuck it under, so the corner is neat and tight. I do the same at each corner. I lay the top sheet wrong side up, then the blanket or cover, and fold the top sheet back over it at the head. I tuck in the foot with mitred corners. I put on the pillowcases, with the open ends facing away from the door, and place the pillows as the standard says. I bend my knees and walk round the bed instead of reaching over.
markingPoints: Checks the mattress and protector; centres the sheet with even overhang
Tucks in at the head and the foot
Describes the mitred corner fold correctly
Top sheet and cover laid and folded back at the head; foot tucked with mitres
Pillowcases open ends away from the door; works safely, bending knees and walking round

essays.stem: Describe how to clean a guest bathroom thoroughly and hygienically.
essays.modelAnswer: I put on gloves and collect my bathroom caddy, with colour-coded cloths and the right chemicals, each read and diluted as the label says. I never mix products, especially bleach with acid or ammonia cleaners, and I keep the extractor fan on or the door open. I remove used towels and rubbish. I flush the toilet and put toilet cleaner under the rim so it can work. I then clean from the cleanest parts to the dirtiest. I clean the mirror and glass shelves, then the basin, taps and counter, then the bath or shower, walls, glass screen and drain, removing hair and limescale. I rinse and dry chrome so it shines without water marks. Then, with the cloth kept only for toilets, I brush the bowl, and clean the seat, lid, hinges, outside and base, and the flush handle. I replace drinking glasses with clean ones. I restock towels, toilet tissue with the end folded, and amenities. Last I clean the floor, working back to the door, and check the room.
markingPoints: Wears gloves and uses chemicals safely, never mixing them, with good airflow
Applies toilet cleaner early so it can work
Cleans from cleanest to dirtiest: mirror, basin, shower, then toilet
Uses toilet cloths for the toilet only and dries chrome to a shine
Replaces glasses, restocks, cleans the floor last and checks

essays.stem: Explain how a stayover (occupied) room service differs from a departure room service, and how you respect the guest's belongings and privacy.
essays.modelAnswer: In a departure room, the guest has gone, so everything is stripped, cleaned and checked for the next guest, and left items are handed in as lost property. In a stayover room the guest is still staying, so the service is lighter and I work round the guest's things. I knock and announce myself, and if the guest is in, I ask if it is a good time. I make the bed, changing the linen only as the property's standard or the guest's green card says. I replace towels left on the floor, empty the bins, clean the bathroom and restock supplies. I do not move or open the guest's luggage, drawers, papers, jewellery, money or medicines; I dust round them. I only throw away what is in the bins. I may fold clothes neatly or leave them, as the rules say. I never read papers, use the phone or TV, or take anything. I keep the door closed and locked while I work away from it, and I never tell anyone who is in the room.
markingPoints: Departure: full strip and clean; left items to lost property
Stayover: lighter service, linen changed as standard or green card says
Knocks and announces; asks the guest if they are in
Does not move, open or read guest belongings; only empties the bins
Keeps the room secure and the guest's details private

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan your day as a room attendant, using the room report.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start of my shift I collect my room report and my key or key card from my supervisor and sign for it. The report lists my rooms and their status, such as departure, stayover, vacant clean, out of order or DND, and any notes like VIP guests, early arrivals or special requests such as a baby cot. I plan the order of my rooms. First I do rooms needed soon, such as early arrivals and VIPs, and departure rooms that the front desk is waiting for. Then I do stayover rooms when the guests are out, often after breakfast, so I do not disturb them. I come back later to rooms with a DND sign and follow the property's rules if the sign stays up. I stock my trolley with enough linen, amenities and chemicals for all my rooms. Through the day I update each room's status as soon as it is finished, and I tell my supervisor about delays, faults or problems.
markingPoints: Collects the room report and keys and understands the status codes
Notes VIPs, early arrivals and special requests
Puts early arrivals, VIPs and needed departures first
Does stayovers when guests are out and handles DND rooms correctly
Stocks the trolley for the day, updates status and reports problems

essays.stem: Explain how a room attendant helps keep guests and their property secure.
essays.modelAnswer: I keep my master key or key card on me at all times, on a cord or clip, and never lend it or leave it in a door or on the trolley. I never let anyone into a room, even if they say it is theirs; I politely send them to the front desk, where their identity can be checked. I never say a guest's name or room number aloud, and I do not tell callers or visitors which room a guest is in. While cleaning, I park my trolley across the open door, and if I leave the room even for a moment I close and lock the door. I do not touch or move the guest's money, jewellery, papers or bags. I check that windows, balcony doors and the room door lock properly when I leave, and I report broken locks or safes. I hand in any lost property straight away so it can be logged. I report strangers in the corridors and anything suspicious to security or my supervisor.
markingPoints: Keeps keys on the person at all times
Never lets anyone into a room; sends them to the front desk to be checked
Keeps guest names and room numbers private
Trolley across the door, locks the door when leaving, checks windows and locks
Leaves valuables alone, hands in lost property and reports suspicious people

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare a villa for a family's arrival, beyond the usual cleaning.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the booking notes for the number of guests, the beds needed, and requests such as a baby cot, extra towels or food allergies. I make sure every bedroom is made up to standard with the right number of pillows and towels, including pool or beach towels. I walk round every room checking that the lights, fans, AC, TV, Wi-Fi card, taps, toilets, hot water, door locks, windows and safe all work, and I report any fault at once so it can be fixed before the family arrives. I check the kitchen is clean and stocked as the villa offers, with glasses and plates clean, and the fridge clean and cold. I put out the welcome basket of local fruit and any welcome drink as close to arrival as I can, keeping food cold. I switch on the AC in good time so the villa is cool, and I spray for mosquitoes only as the property allows. Last, I check the pool area is safe, the gate closes, and I walk through as a guest would.
markingPoints: Reads booking notes and special requests
Prepares beds, towels and extras for the number of guests
Checks that all equipment works and reports faults quickly
Prepares the kitchen and welcome items, keeping food fresh and cold
Cools the villa in time, checks pool safety and does a final walk-through

essays.stem: Explain the main health and safety risks a room attendant faces, and how to work safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Back injury is a big risk, because a room attendant makes many beds and pushes a heavy trolley. I bend my knees, keep my back straight, walk round the bed instead of reaching across, and get help with heavy mattresses. Chemicals can burn the skin and eyes or give off gas. I read the label and SDS, measure dilutions, wear gloves and eye protection where needed, keep rooms aired and never mix products such as bleach with acid or ammonia cleaners. Sharps such as needles and broken glass can be hidden in bins and bedding, so I strip beds slowly, never push rubbish down with my hand, and report needles for the sharps box. Body fluids can carry germs, so I use gloves and the spill kit as the rules say. Wet bathroom floors cause slips, so I wear non-slip shoes and dry floors. I check electrical items such as vacuums, kettles and lamps, and report faults. I also take breaks and drink water in hot weather.
markingPoints: Manual handling: bend knees, walk round the bed, get help
Chemicals: label and SDS, dilution, PPE, airflow, never mix
Sharps and body fluids: strip slowly, do not push rubbish down, report, use gloves and spill kit
Slips: non-slip shoes and dry floors
Electrical checks and looking after themselves in the heat

essays.stem: Describe how to carry out an evening turn-down service in a hotel room.
essays.modelAnswer: Turn-down is done in the early evening, often while guests are at dinner. I check the room report for rooms that want the service and for special requests. I knock, say "Housekeeping", wait and repeat, and if the guest is in, I ask if they would like turn-down now or later. I empty the bins and remove used room-service trays and glasses. I tidy the room without moving the guest's belongings. I fold back the top of the bed cover or duvet at an angle on the side the guest sleeps, and plump the pillows. I place the bedside mat or slippers, and the chocolate, card or breakfast menu, as the property's standard says. I close the curtains, switch on the bedside lamp and set the AC to a comfortable level, as the standard says. In the bathroom I replace used towels, wipe the basin and refill tissue and amenities. I check the room, close and lock the door, and record that the service is done.
markingPoints: Done in the early evening; checks the report and requests
Correct entry and asks the guest if present
Empties bins, removes trays and tidies without moving belongings
Turns back the bed, places amenities, closes curtains and sets lights and AC
Freshens the bathroom, locks the door and records the service

essays.stem: Describe how to set up and stock a room attendant's trolley, and explain why it matters.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start of the shift I check my room report to see how many rooms I have and what type they are, so I know how much to take. I check the trolley is clean, the wheels run well and the dirty linen bag and rubbish bag are empty and fixed in place. I put heavy items such as stacks of sheets on the bottom shelf so the trolley does not tip, and towels and pillowcases on the middle shelf. Guest amenities, toilet tissue and stationery go on the top shelf in their places. Chemicals and cleaning cloths go in a separate caddy, kept apart from clean linen and amenities, with every bottle labelled and closed. I add my vacuum, signs and gloves. I record the stock I take from the linen room. A well-set trolley matters because it saves trips, keeps clean items clean, keeps chemicals safe and away from guests, and stops the trolley tipping. Through the day I keep it tidy, and at the end I restock it and store it in the linen room.
markingPoints: Uses the room report to plan quantities
Checks the trolley and fits the linen and rubbish bags
Heavy items low; linen and amenities in set places
Chemicals labelled, closed and kept apart from clean items
Records stock and explains why the set-up matters, then restocks at the end

practical1.title: Service a departure room in the mock villa
practical1.brief: As a group, prepare a bedroom and bathroom of the Centre's mock villa (or a training bedroom) after a guest has checked out, to the standard of a Jamaican villa or hotel. The assessor sets up the room as a guest left it, with used linen, towels, rubbish, an item left behind and one fault (for example a bulb that does not work), and acts as your supervisor. Work in these stages: (1) read the room report and stock the trolley; (2) enter correctly, air the room and check for left items, damage and faults; (3) strip the bed, check the mattress and make the bed with fresh linen and mitred corners; (4) clean the bathroom from the cleanest parts to the toilet, and the floor last; (5) restock towels, toilet tissue and amenities; (6) dust from high to low, clean the mirrors and check the equipment; (7) vacuum, working back to the door; (8) check the room as a guest would, fill in the lost property and maintenance forms, lock the room and update its status. Share the stages so every member strips or makes part of the bed and cleans part of the bathroom while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Room attendant's trolley with linen bag and rubbish bag
Clean bed linen: sheets, pillowcases, cover or duvet, and mattress protector
Towels, bath mat, toilet tissue and guest amenities
Bathroom caddy with colour-coded cloths, toilet brush and bathroom chemicals, with labels and SDS
Room report, lost property form and maintenance form
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The trolley stocked and parked across the door
The room as found, with the left item and the fault
The stripped bed, with the mattress checked
The made bed, close up of a mitred corner
The finished bathroom, with towels and amenities in place
The finished bedroom seen from the door
The completed lost property and maintenance forms and the updated room report
checklist: Knocked, announced and waited before entering
Found the left item and the fault and reported them on the right forms
Stripped the bed carefully, looking for sharps and guest items
Made the bed neatly to standard with tight mitred corners
Used chemicals safely and kept the toilet cloth for the toilet only
Cleaned the bathroom in the right order and restocked to standard
Dusted high to low and vacuumed last
Checked the room, locked it and updated its status
Used safe lifting and bending, and took a full part in the group
safety: Strip beds slowly; never pick up needles or broken glass by hand; tell the assessor
Read labels, wear gloves, keep the bathroom aired and never mix chemicals; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Bend your knees and walk round the bed; get help to lift the mattress
Keep the trolley across the door and the vacuum cable out of walkways
Wipe up water on the bathroom floor at once

practical2.title: Stayover service and evening turn-down for an occupied villa room
practical2.brief: As a group, give a stayover service and then an evening turn-down to a bedroom of the Centre's mock villa that a guest is still using. The assessor sets out the guest's belongings (clothes, a bag, papers, a phone charger, jewellery made of plastic) and a green card on one bed, and plays the guest for part of the time. Work in these stages: (1) read the room report and the guest's requests; (2) enter correctly and ask the guest, if present, whether it is a good time; (3) make the beds, changing the linen only as the green card and the standard say, and make one bed with a duvet; (4) clean and restock the bathroom, replacing only the towels the guest has left out; (5) tidy and dust round the guest's belongings without moving or opening them; (6) empty the bins and vacuum; (7) later, give turn-down: fold back the bed, place the amenities, close the curtains, set the lights and AC, and freshen the bathroom; (8) lock the room and record both services. Every member takes part in the bed making and in either the bathroom or the turn-down, while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.

Bathroom caddy with colour-coded cloths and chemicals, with labels and SDS
Turn-down items: a card or chocolate, bedside mat or slippers, breakfast menu
Guest belongings and a green card, set out by the assessor
A phone or camera for the photos

checklist: Entered correctly and spoke politely to the guest
Followed the green card and the standard for linen changes
Made the duvet bed and the other bed neatly to standard
Did not move, open or read the guest's belongings, and only emptied the bins
Cleaned and restocked the bathroom correctly and safely
Gave turn-down to the property's standard
Kept the room door closed and locked when away from it
Recorded both services on the room report
Worked safely and took a full part in the group
safety: Read labels, wear gloves and never mix chemicals; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
Bend your knees when making beds and get help with heavy duvets or mattresses
Keep the vacuum cable out of the way, and switch off and unplug it after use
Wipe up water on the bathroom floor at once
Keep the room locked when you step out
